trades.name: VVV
trades.why: Same-store sales of 9.4%, a fiscal 2027 guide for 8% profit growth and a buyback raised to $500M (about a tenth of the company) took it up 10% on three times normal volume on a day 446 S&P names fell, and it gave back only 0.7% after hours.
trades.wrong_if: Two or more covering brokers downgrade Valvoline after the print, or Valvoline says its 10-K will be late or discloses a new material weakness, or it lowers the fiscal 2027 guide or says same-store sales have slowed this quarter, inside the window.
trades.stood_down: passed: spread wider than 2% (VVV 14.0%, XRT 25.4%) when it was due to enter

trades.name: WSM
trades.why: A one-cent beat with the year's guide only repeated cost it 15% on 4.4 times volume and a close near the low; hitting that guide now needs a strong holiday quarter that management itself described as later, more promotional and with housing worse, so the estimate and target cuts are still to come.
trades.wrong_if: Two or more covering brokers upgrade Williams-Sonoma after the print, or the company raises its fiscal 2026 guide, announces an accelerated buyback, or says holiday demand is running ahead of plan, inside the window.
trades.stood_down: passed: spread wider than 2% (XRT 25.4%, WSM 7.7%) when it was due to enter

trades.name: INTU
trades.why: Intuit cut Credit Karma's growth to 3-7% from 11-13% and said consumers are starting in AI tools instead, and guided Q2 revenue about 3% under consensus: the first large software company to put a number on the AI fear, in the week that fear is the story, with the estimate cuts still to come.
trades.wrong_if: Two or more covering brokers upgrade Intuit on valuation after the print, or Intuit announces an accelerated share repurchase or a larger buyback, or management restores the Credit Karma outlook at an investor event, inside the window.

trades.name: ACN
trades.why: Accenture lost about 12% in three sessions on no company news, sits on its 50-day, and is turning today with Cognizant and IBM on a day chips are sold again: the same chips-down, services-up rotation that lifted the group in October.
trades.wrong_if: A frontier AI lab (Anthropic, OpenAI or Google) launches a product aimed at consulting or IT-services work and the group sells off on it; or two or more covering brokers downgrade Accenture; or Accenture trims its FY27 guide; or on a session when SMH rises 3% or more, ACN, CTSH and IBM all close lower (the rotation reversing), inside the window.

trades.name: TAK
trades.why: A new 52-week high on 1.6x volume on a day Tokyo fell 5% and New York 2%, in a stock re-rating on three launches with the US narcolepsy launch cleared eight days ago and a new CEO's targets due 12-11.
trades.wrong_if: Takeda or a regulator (FDA, PMDA) announces a safety action, label restriction, supply problem or launch delay on Orzeyful or Mimrylo; or Takeda lowers its FY2026 guidance or moves or cancels the 12-11 Capital Markets Day; or two or more covering brokers downgrade it, inside the window.

trades.name: MTZ
trades.why: MasTec fell 12% to a 52-week low on announcing a $1.25B debt-funded acquisition two weeks after it shelved deal talks to favour a buyback, on top of an October guidance cut: a credibility break with a named cause, not just the tape.
trades.wrong_if: Two or more covering brokers upgrade MasTec or raise their price targets citing the Murphy deal; or MasTec announces a larger or accelerated buyback, or directors or officers report open-market purchases (Form 4); or MasTec changes the financing so the deal adds less debt, inside the window.
